title: fix(scripts): judge a dotted callee by its receiver as well as its last segment
body:
Fixes #18643

`descentRoots()` in `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` decides whether a call starts a directory descent by matching the callee against `NON_DESCENT_CALLEES`, and the match takes the callee's LAST dotted segment. That is the right question for a METHOD row — `path.join(...)` pops to `join` — and the wrong one for an OBJECT row: `JSON.stringify(PATH_EXPR)` pops to `stringify`, so the `'JSON'` row could only ever match a bare `JSON(...)` call, a form the corpus does not contain. The first argument of every missed call entered as a candidate walk root.

Clause-②: no — a repo gate script only; nothing published moves (measured below).

## The fix

A dotted callee is now asked both questions: its last segment against `NON_DESCENT_CALLEES`, its receiver against a new `NON_DESCENT_NAMESPACES`. Every name in the new set is already a row in the old one, and the receiver leg runs for DOTTED callees only — so a bare call is judged exactly as before. It reads the FIRST segment only, so a rostered name in a middle segment (`x.JSON.stringify(dir)`) is still a descent. The safe direction is unchanged: an unlisted name is still treated as a descent.

## Card question 1 — which rows are live and which are dead, row by row

Measured over the 3733 test files this gate scans, on this repo at `8904880601`, at the gate's own grain (a raw text scan, comments included). "bare" = matches the roster can still catch; "receiver missed" = dotted call sites where the row is the receiver and the last-segment match walks past it.

| row | bare | receiver missed | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `JSON` | 8 | 3220 | DEAD — all 8 bare hits are the word in a comment or a message; zero real `JSON(...)` calls |
| `Object` | 4 | 4451 | DEAD — all 4 bare hits are prose (`'Object (type)'`, `'Object (en-US)'`, one comment) |
| `vi` | 0 | 10835 | DEAD outright — never reached at all, in either position |
| `Array` | 13 | 1509 | LIVE bare (real `Array(n)` / `new Array(n)` calls), blind to `Array.from(...)` |
| `String` | 4019 | 17 | LIVE bare, blind to `String.raw(...)` and siblings |
| `Number` | 412 | 70 | LIVE bare, blind to `Number.isInteger(...)` and siblings |
| `Boolean` | 54 | 0 | LIVE bare; no dotted use in the corpus |
| `Set` | 1139 | 0 | LIVE bare; no dotted use in the corpus |
| `Map` | 610 | 0 | LIVE bare; no dotted use in the corpus |
| `require` | 52 | 0 | LIVE bare; `require.resolve(...)` was already caught, by the `resolve` row |
| `import` | 704 | 0 | LIVE bare; `import.meta.resolve(...)` likewise |
| `expect` | 133356 | 1076 | LIVE bare, blind to `expect.any(...)` |
| `it` | 52709 | 1158 | LIVE bare, blind to `it.each(...)` |
| `describe` | 12885 | 113 | LIVE bare, blind to `describe.each(...)` |
| `test` | 424 | 4 | LIVE bare, blind to `test.each(...)` |

The method-named rows (`join`, `resolve`, `dirname`, `readFileSync`, …) were never in question: they are matched wherever they sit, and this change keeps that.

So the fix is not JSON-shaped: all sixteen object-named rows are now asked about as receivers. `URL` is in the new set for the same reason (`URL.canParse(...)`); `fs` and `path` deliberately are not — their methods are rows in the old set, and a namespace whose members read the filesystem does not belong in the new one.

## Card question 2 — does fixing it turn the gate red? No

The gate's own output is byte-identical before and after, exit 0 on both:

```
OK: 29 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared, and turbo.json hashes every declared glob (6 of them on a split "test:repo" task); 13 walked root(s) judged, 3 on ACCEPTED_WALK_RADII; 2020 test file(s) import a workspace sibling by bare specifier over 349 package pair(s), every one declared.
```

At the descent scan's own grain the corpus does move: raw walk roots go 26 (over 18 files) to 23 (over 16). The three that disappear are all a path handed to `JSON.stringify` inside a template literal building a shell command:

| file | root withdrawn | call site |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` | `packages/spec/package.json` | `cp ${JSON.stringify(join(SPEC_PKG, 'package.json'))} …` |
| `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` | `packages/spec/dist` | `ln -s ${JSON.stringify(join(SPEC_PKG, 'dist'))} …` |
| `packages/spec/scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-cleanup.test.ts` | `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh` | `` source ${JSON.stringify(SCRIPT)} `` |

None of them ever reached the walk limb's judgement — a build output is untracked and the other two are files, both filtered by the tracked-directory criterion — which is why 13 judged roots stay 13 and no declaration becomes stale. The first two are the pair the card relays from PR #18641; the third is new here and the same shape.

## The two acceptance controls

Both legs are the same `walkRootsOf` probe, run against a detached worktree at `origin/main` and against this branch, on samples that all carry the anonymous descent the walk limb needs before it engages at all.

| sample | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| LIT `JSON.stringify(join(REPO, 'content'))` | `["content"]` | `[]` |
| LIT `Object.keys(...)` | `["content"]` | `[]` |
| LIT `Array.from(...)` | `["content"]` | `[]` |
| LIT `vi.mock(...)` | `["content"]` | `[]` |
| LIT `expect.any(...)` | `["content"]` | `[]` |
| DARK bare `String(...)` | `[]` | `[]` |
| DARK bare `require(...)` | `[]` | `[]` |
| DARK bare `Number(...)` | `[]` | `[]` |
| DARK `new Set(...)` | `[]` | `[]` |
| CONTROL bare `stringify(...)` — unrostered | `["content"]` | `["content"]` |
| CONTROL `helper.crawl(...)` — unrostered, dotted | `["content"]` | `["content"]` |
| CONTROL `x.JSON.stringify(...)` — rostered name in a middle segment | `["content"]` | `["content"]` |
| CONTROL `walk(...)` — the descent itself | `["content"]` | `["content"]` |
| CONTROL `path.join(...)` alone | `[]` | `[]` |
| CONTROL `fs.readdirSync(...)` — a rostered method, dotted | `[]` | `[]` |

The DARK rows read `[]` on both legs, which on its own is what a scan that stopped answering would also print — the four positive controls beside them are what make that reading mean something.

## Ablation — the new battery can fail

Committed first, then the receiver leg alone was deleted from `descentRoots`, proven on disk (anchor count 1 to 0; blob `7d0df32f` to `2362a7df`), and the self-test re-run:

```
ABLATED SELF-TEST EXIT = 1
FAIL LIT: `JSON.stringify(PATH_EXPR)` is not a descent -- the reported shape
FAIL LIT: `Object.keys(PATH_EXPR)` is not a descent
FAIL LIT: `Array.from(PATH_EXPR)` is not a descent
FAIL LIT: `vi.mock(PATH_EXPR)` is not a descent
FAIL LIT: `expect.any(PATH_EXPR)` is not a descent
5/229 self-test case(s) failed.
```

Five LIT legs red, every DARK leg and every control still green. Restored from `HEAD` and proven restored: on-disk blob back to `7d0df32f`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` clean.

## What was run

- `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` — self-test 214 cases before, 229 after (the new battery is 15), exit 0; verify exit 0 on both legs with identical output.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 30 families for this change set; all 30 run, all exit 0, reconciled with `--ran` (30 derived, 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN). Includes `check:nul-bytes`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:self-test-wired`, `check:published-list-mirrors`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`.
- Lint, narrowed and declared: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the one changed file — 1 file linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings, at `5d4a7db5b9`. The narrowing excludes nothing: the population `pnpm lint` covers is 6837 files (ESLint's own config — the global block's extension glob over 8862 tracked files, none of them ignored by `eslint.isPathIgnored`), and `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting for any file (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules — stated and positively controlled in its own header), so a one-file `.mjs` edit cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide scan itself is CI's.
- No package build or package test is owed: the diff touches one file in the private root package, and every reference to it in a test source is a comment — no test imports or reads it. Four packages (`cli`, `plugin-auth`, `trigger-record-change`, `plugin-approvals`) name it in their `test` inputs in turbo.json, so CI re-runs those suites on the moved hash; that half is declared to CI and was not run locally.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, measured rather than inferred: the package that owns `scripts/` is the repo root, `private: true` with no `files[]`, and of the 70 manifests that declare `files[]`, zero name a `scripts` directory — against a positive control of 70 that name `dist`. Nothing published moves.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:

- `turbo.json` names `$TURBO_ROOT$/scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` in the `test` inputs of `@objectstack/trigger-record-change` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` while their declared radius is a `packages/runtime/src/...` file; `cli` and `plugin-auth` name the declaration module `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` beside it. The gate's verify limb is green either way, so this is an inconsistency in what the two hash, not a defect — and the next PR to touch those rows is the one that would see it.
